Polycyclic groups and collectors

Source: R/combinatorics-fpgroups.R
PolycyclicGroup.Rd

perm_polycyclic_group(G) returns the polycyclic group of a solvable permutation group G (SymPy's G.polycyclic_group()), with its polycyclic generating sequence $pcgs, series $pc_series, relative orders $relative_order and Collector $collector. The collector's $pc_presentation is an ordered dictionary of power and conjugate relations; pc_presentation() lists it as pairs. collected_word(), exponent_vector(), pc_depth(), leading_exponent(), induced_pcgs(), constructive_membership_test(), minimal_uncollected_subword() and pc_relations() are the methods of SymPy's Collector.

Usage

PolycyclicGroup(pc_sequence, pc_series, relative_order, collector = NULL)

perm_polycyclic_group(G)

pc_is_prime_order(PC)

pc_length(PC)

Collector(
  pcgs,
  pc_series,
  relative_order,
  free_group_ = NULL,
  pc_presentation_ = NULL
)

pc_presentation(C)

minimal_uncollected_subword(C, word)

pc_relations(C)

collected_word(C, word)

exponent_vector(C, element)

pc_depth(C, element)

leading_exponent(C, element)

induced_pcgs(C, gens)

constructive_membership_test(C, ipcgs, g)

Arguments

pc_sequence, pcgs

A list of permutations.

pc_series

A list of permutation groups.

relative_order

An integer vector.

collector

A collector (made when NULL).

G

A solvable permutation group.

PC

A polycyclic group.

free_group_, pc_presentation_

Optional free group and presentation.

C

A collector.

word

A word of the collector's free group.

element

A permutation.

gens, ipcgs

Lists of permutations.

g

A permutation.

Value

A PolycyclicGroup, a Collector, a word, a list or an integer.

Examples

PC <- perm_polycyclic_group(SymmetricGroup(4))
PC$relative_order
#> [1] 2 3 2 2
exponent_vector(PC$collector, SymmetricGroup(4)$gens[[1]])
#> [1] 1 0 0 0
